Light / geometry / art

Shadow Printing

An experiment in using light, shadow and geometry as a printing process.

Idea

Light doing the printing.

Using light, shadow and geometry as a printing process. Playful, with real constraints - the physics decides what is possible, the setup decides whether you can repeat it.

Product thought

Print the object, reveal the image.

The toy version is a small piece of software that starts with a picture and generates printable blocks. In ordinary light they are just strange geometry; with a torch or the sun in the right place, the shadow becomes the image. It is part CAD problem, part optics problem, part "will this still work on a kitchen table?" problem.

Variant

A clock made from shadows.

The same idea also wandered into a clock: digits or hands cast as shadows rather than printed on a face. Names considered in the old notes included LightCast and TimeInShadows, which is exactly the level of overthinking a shadow-clock deserves.

Shadow Printing Optics, geometry and repeatability.
